name: Edge node update corruption
blurb: Cover for hardware and operational failure when a patch corrupts distributed edge nodes.
summary: Cover for hardware and operational failure when a patch corrupts distributed edge nodes.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: A broad cyber exclusion that bars coverage for any failure of computer systems, including non malicious operational errors like a faulty patch, would defeat this exposure.
An exclusion for inherent vice, latent defect, or faulty workmanship that could be applied to a software update that corrupts hardware.
A sublimit for electronic data processing equipment that is far below the replacement cost of all edge nodes, leaving most hardware uninsured.
A business interruption waiting period of seventy two hours or more that would eliminate coverage for short duration update failures that are common in edge networks.
An exclusion for loss of use, loss of data, or loss of access that would deny business interruption claims when the update corruption does not cause physical damage to hardware.
A contractual liability exclusion that removes coverage for service level agreement penalties and liquidated damages, which are the primary third party exposure.
A professional services or errors and omissions exclusion in the commercial general liability policy that pushes all update related liability to a separate technology policy with lower limits.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Delete the inherent vice, latent defect, and faulty workmanship exclusions for software updates so that corruption of edge nodes is a covered cause of loss.
Add an endorsement that defines a faulty software update or patch as a covered peril for both property damage and business interruption.
Include data restoration and reinstallation costs as covered extra expense, with a sublimit of at least one million dollars per event.
Carve back the contractual liability exclusion to cover service level agreement penalties and liquidated damages up to a negotiated sublimit.
Remove any broad cyber exclusion language that could be interpreted to exclude non malicious operational errors like a corrupted update.
Add contingent business interruption coverage for loss of income when a corrupted edge node causes an outage for a customer that depends on that node.
Negotiate a rollback and emergency patch deployment expense endorsement that covers the cost of restoring nodes to a previous stable version.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: A waiting period of eight to twelve hours is negotiated instead of the standard twenty four to seventy two hours because edge node operators promise high availability and short recovery times.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption coverage includes lost revenue and extra expense for the period of restoration, with a sublimit for contingent business interruption when a corrupted update at one node causes downstream customer outages.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Electronic data processing equipment coverage is written as a separate sublimit, typically five million to ten million dollars, but must be endorsed to include damage caused by faulty software updates and not just named perils.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Primary property limit is set at the full replacement cost of the largest single edge node cluster, typically ten million to twenty five million dollars per occurrence, with excess layers stacked to the total insurable value of all edge nodes.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: A typical primary commercial general liability limit of one million dollars per occurrence and two million dollars aggregate, but for edge node operators with large customer contracts underwriters often require a five million dollar primary or a fronting arrangement.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Claims made for the technology errors and omissions liability portion because update corruption is a latent defect that may not manifest until after the policy period; first party property damage is written on an occurrence basis.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess liability towers are built in layers of five million to twenty five million dollars, with total limits driven by the largest customer contract penalty and the number of edge nodes; a fifty million dollar tower is common for regional providers while hyperscale edge networks may require one hundred million dollars or more.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Customer claims for business interruption and lost profits when a corrupted update causes edge node downtime that breaches service level agreements.
Data corruption or loss on edge nodes leading to privacy breach notifications and regulatory fines under data protection laws.
Negligence claims from customers alleging the insured failed to properly test or stage the update before deployment.
Contractual liability for penalties, service credits, or liquidated damages triggered by update related outages.
Third party property damage or bodily injury if corrupted edge nodes control physical infrastructure such as traffic systems, medical devices, or industrial equipment.
Downstream liability to end users of customer applications that rely on the edge nodes for processing or storage.
Intellectual property or licensing disputes if the corrupted update causes unauthorized access or alteration of third party software.

underwriter_wants_to_know: What is the patch management and change control process for edge node updates, including testing and rollback procedures?
How many edge nodes are deployed, where are they located, and what is the total replacement cost of the hardware at risk?
What redundancy or failover architecture exists so that a corrupted update does not take down all nodes simultaneously?
What contractual obligations and service level agreements exist with customers that could trigger penalties or liability after an update failure?
Has the insured experienced any prior update corruption events, and what was the financial impact and recovery time?
Are edge nodes used to control physical equipment or safety critical systems where a failure could cause bodily injury or property damage to third parties?
What vendor warranties or indemnities apply to the software patches, and does the insured have recourse against the software vendor?
